es-b1-listen-discusion.role: Phase 8.1 B1-extension Unit 23 sustained listening passage — a two-voice opinion discussion rendered entirely by on-device speech synthesis at lesson time (no audio file is shipped)
es-b1-listen-discusion.declaredUrl: n/a — no recording; the passage lives as four section texts in Condisco/Content/packs/spanish.json under sustainedListenings (id es-b1-listen-discusion)
es-b1-listen-discusion.transcript: The full four-section text (Marta ↔ Iker) as authored in the pack's transcript field; section texts are the same words the synthesizer speaks.
es-b1-listen-discusion.note: Declared voice ids are preferences, not requirements: when a declared identifier is not installed on the learner's device, the section is spoken by any installed voice whose language matches the section's languageCode (documented on SustainedListeningSection.voiceId in Condisco/Models/CoursePack.swift). A missing voice can never make a section unspeakable. Voice availability varies by device and iOS version, so no static audio hash exists.

sequence: es-b1-listen-discusion — presented by the new step es-b1-opinion-listen-step-listen (purpose notice, sustainedListeningId es-b1-listen-discusion, launch activity es-b1-listen-discusion-launch) between step-write and the read step; the lesson terminal is the recall step. The view lane hides the transcript on the first pass, offers per-section replay at normal/slow speed, reveals the transcript on demand, and grades the three embedded questions (main idea / key detail / speaker intent) with fixed-answer selection logic, the same 6.1 pattern as es-sustained-listen-llamada.
delivery: device-speech — intentionally NOT shipped as a recording. AudioStimulus-style on-device AVSpeechSynthesizer rendering from the authored section texts; the passage is a data-level construct (sections + voice ids + transcript), so no entry is needed in tools/device-speech-media.txt (that allowlist covers MediaItem assets; this passage declares no media items).

generator.voice: per-section declared voice id when installed; otherwise any installed voice of the section's language (es-ES / es-MX), falling back to the system Spanish voice
generator.note: Not a fixed file voice: output varies by device and voice availability, so no static audio hash exists.
